legend: You are given n%%ZSMJ0%% intervals [li,ri]%%ZSMJ1%%, where li≤ri%%ZSMJ2%%. Your task is to determine if there exist n%%ZSMJ3%% integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ4%% satisfying:
input: The first line contains an integer t%%ZSMJ10%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ11%%), the number of test cases.
The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ12%% (2≤n≤105%%ZSMJ13%%) denoting the number of intervals.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ14%% integers l1,l2,…,ln%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤li≤106%%ZSMJ16%%).
The third line contains n%%ZSMJ17%% integers r1,r2,…,rn%%ZSMJ18%% (li≤ri≤106%%ZSMJ19%%).
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ20%% over all test cases does not exceed 105%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: YES if it is possible to choose x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ22%% such that it satisfies the constraints. On the next line, output n%%ZSMJ23%% space-separated integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ24%%.
The letters in the word YES and NO are case insensitive. For example, YES, yeS and No are all considered valid.
note: In the first example, we choose 5%%ZSMJ25%%, 5%%ZSMJ26%% and 10%%ZSMJ27%% respectively from each range. Then, we have gcd(5,5,10)=5≠1%%ZSMJ28%%.
In the second example, it is not possible to choose n%%ZSMJ29%% integers satisfying the condition.
